reason: The cited evidence directly states that CrCoNi has a lower-energy hcp phase and that magnetically frustrated Mn eliminates the fcc-hcp energy difference, and it explicitly links the transformation to dislocation activity. These statements accurately support all key premises of the hypothesis without contradiction or overstatement.
premises: CrCoNi has a lower-energy hcp phase relative to fcc, enabling a magnetically tunable fcc-to-hcp transformation during deformation.
Magnetically frustrated Mn in the quinary CrMnFeCoNi alloy eliminates the fcc-hcp energy difference, suppressing the transformation.
The fcc-to-hcp transformation in CrCoNi is triggered by dislocation slip and interaction with internal boundaries.
The presence or absence of this transformation explains the different mechanical properties between the quinary and Mn-free/reduced alloys.
